Judgment
1.
This case has arisen out of accident which occurred on 06.12.2015 at Samalka Red Light near NSG Camp Link Road, Dwarka, New Delhi.
The cause of accident was rash/negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-79-3470 (car) which rendered a person dead and another person injured.
The person who died is Pradeep Kumar and the person who suffered injury is Sonu.
The police registered an FIR and investigated the matter.
The police has also presented a DAR for the purpose of compensation.
The legal- heirs of Pradeep Kumar has filed claim petition for the purpose of compensation.
DAR was tagged with the claim petition.
Owner of the vehicle is Rajesh Kumar S/o Ganga Dutt and the driver is Rajesh Kumar S/o Attar Singh.
The vehicle was insured with an insurance Insurance.

2. The driver and owner appeared and filed joint reply contending that the driver was driving the vehicle properly and deceased was driving the motorcycle rashly and negligently and deceased was not wearing helmet.
The insurance company also filed reply.

On the basis of available material, the Ld. Predecessor framed following issues:
RAKESH 1.

Whether Pradeep Kumar sustained fatal injuries KUMAR SINGH in a motor vehicle accident dtd. 06.12.2015 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle (Car) no. HR Date: 2025.12.05 79 3470 being driven by Rajesh Kumar, owned by 18:22:46 +0530 Rajessh Kumar and insured by IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co.
Ltd. ?
Whther
the petititioners are entititled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

...OPP 3. Relief.
3.
During the evidence, Poonam Devi, Prem Singh, Sonu @ Vikas, Ashish Tigala and Inspector Yakub Khan were examined from the side of claimants.
No witness has been examined from the side of respondents.
Both the sides have been heard.
This judgment will disposed off the case.

sentences.text: 4. Occurrence of accident has been mentioned in the FIR and charge-sheet.
Involvement of the offending vehicle is also mentioned so.
In terms of Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals Rules 2008, the FIR and charge-sheet have to be accepted for their contents.

sentences.text: 5. The driver has claimed that he was driving in proper Digitally signed by manner.
This claim itself shows that the offending vehicle was RAKESH RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR SINGH present at the spot.

Once, the charge-sheet has found the driver as SINGH Date:
2025.12.05 18:22:52 culprit, a prima-facie presumption can be taken that offending +0530 driver was rash/negligent.

It was then for the driver to dispute the rashness/
negligence.
The driver/owner have not led any evidence to support the proper driving.
Once this is so, there is no reason as to why the contents of charge-sheet should not be accepted.

If the insurance company was of the view that deceased was solely negligent, it should have appointed its own investigator to investigate the accident and should have led evidence in support of its claim.
The insurance company has done neither.
It is clear that accident happened due to rash/ negligent driving of Rajesh Kumar.
Issue No. 1 is decided in favour of claimants.
6. On the point of compensation, it needs to be noted that the accident resulted into death of a person and therefore, the compensation has to be given on the settled principles for calculation.
7. The age of deceased Pradeep Kumar was 28 years at the time of accident and the respondents have not been able to dispute this fact.
Therefore, age is accepted.

The multiplier will be 17.
8.

So far as income of deceased is concerned, the claim made by the wife of deceased is that deceased was working as a Supervisor in Ambiance Company, Gurgaon, Haryana and was RAKESH getting Rs.12,000/- per month.
She further states that petitioners KUMAR SINGH were completely dependent on his income.
However, no witness has been brought in support of the claim regarding monthly Date: 2025.12.05 income.
Deceased was however a matriculate and therefore, I am 18:22:57 +0530 of the view that atleast minimum wages of matriculate person in Haryana should be taken as income.

The minimum wages on the date of accident was Rs.8,379/-.
9.
Since the deceased was 28 years of age, there will be addition of 40% as future prospect as he was not employed in permanent job.
There were six dependents and therefore, 1/4 th shall be deducted towards personal expenses.
10. The loss of income, therefore, shall be Rs.8,379/- x 12 x 17 which will be equal to Rs.17,09,316/-.
The future prospect will come to Rs.6,83,726.4/-.
After deduction on personal expenses at 1/4th, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.17,94,781.8/-.

11. On account loss of consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses, fixed sum of Rs.2,90,400/-,
Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/- are allowed, as there are six dependents.

sentences.text: There is nothing on record to justify withholding interest on the award amount.
Therefore, a simple interest @ 7.5 % per annum is allowed on the Award Amount w.e.f. 10.05.2016 till realization.
If any interim compensation was paid the same shall be deducted from the final compensation.
13. Out of the total amount, the wife shall get 35%, the children shall get 15% each and the parents shall get 10% each.
The disbursement shall be through the award.

Liability 14. Respondent no.1 Rakesh Kumar S/o Attar Singh (driver) being principal tortfeasor driving the vehicle no. HR-79-3470 in rash/ negligent manner without proper vigil resulting in accident leading to death is primarily liable.
The Rajesh Kumar S/o Ganga Dutt being owner of the vehicle is vicariously liable.

However, since offending vehicle was insured with the insurance company against third party risk so, Insurance Company (insurer) being statutorily liable under Section 150 of M.V.
Act shall pay the award amount with interest to petitioners.
15. Let a separate Award be prepared based on the aforesaid calculation and directions, so that all the concerned persons can comply with the same.
